fields.h1: Build an Influencer Application Form That Sorts Every Applicant
fields.hero_description: Build an influencer application form that saves each creator's handles, audience, and rate in a database you own.
fields.features_heading: Everything Needed to Say Yes to a Creator
fields.features_subheading: An influencer application form built in Emergent collects the details to check before you send product or pay a rate.
fields.feature_1:
One row for each platform

Applicants add a row for every platform they post on, with the handle and the follower count side by side. A creator on Instagram and TikTok fills in two rows, not one crowded box.
fields.feature_2:
Media kits and sample posts as uploads

Ask for a media kit and links to three recent sponsored posts. The files are saved with the application, and the reviewer sees past work without writing to the creator to ask for it.
fields.feature_3:
A rate field with a ceiling you set

Ask for a rate per deliverable, such as one Reel or one Story. A rate above the ceiling goes to a named approver by email or in Slack, and every other one goes to the shortlist.
fields.feature_4:
Dates with a fixed number of spots

Offer hosted dates or event slots, each with a set number of creator spots. Once the last spot on a date is taken, the form hides that date from the next applicant who opens it.
fields.feature_5:
Disclosure terms signed in the form

Close the form with your disclosure and usage terms and a typed or drawn signature. The signed terms are stored with the signing date and the application, in a database you own.
fields.feature_6:
Code a developer can take further

Export the code for the form and its review screens to your GitHub repository on paid plans. A developer can host it on your own servers or keep building on it from there.

fields.usecase_heading: How Four Brands Act on Each Application
fields.tab_content_1:
One seeding list, made from approved applications

Mossgrove Skincare ships a box of new products to a few creators each month. Mirela Szabo applies with 14,200 Instagram followers, combination skin, and a shipping address. Tamsin Okoro approves her, and the address moves to the March seeding list that Tamsin packs boxes from.
fields.tab_content_2:
The director signs off on any rate over $1,500

Strideline Running pays creators for its spring campaign, and every application asks for a rate. Teodor Lisk asks $2,400 for 1 Reel and 2 Stories and attaches his media kit. Any rate over $1,500 goes to Eleanor Rusk, the marketing director, by email before anyone replies to him.
fields.tab_content_3:
A weekend closes when its second creator applies

Pelican Rock Inn hosts 2 travel creators per weekend in return for coverage of the stay. Anouk Bastien takes the second spot on the November 14 weekend and links 2 past hotel stays she covered. The form stops offering that weekend, and Hollis Tran, the general manager, gets her application in Slack.
fields.tab_content_4:
The signed #ad terms come back with the application

Fernbrook Tea ends its application with its terms: #ad in the caption of every post, and 90 days of paid usage for each video. Wilhelmina Oduya signs them with a drawn signature. When Briar Okonkwo opens the application, the signed terms and their date sit above the approve button.

fields.howto_title: How to Create an Influencer Application Form
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to create an influencer application form that collects what you check before saying yes, then routes each applicant.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 Write down what you will give creators
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Set a minimum audience per platform
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 Ask for the rate in one unit
fields.howto_step_1_des: Decide whether the program sends free product, pays a rate, or hosts a stay. Each offer changes the questions. A seeding program needs a shipping address and no rate, while a paid campaign needs deliverables and a price before anything else.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Pick the smallest audience you will work with on each platform and put that question first. An applicant below the line on every platform they list sees a short thank-you screen instead of the rest of the form.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Choose one unit for rates, for example a single Reel or a 60-second video, and ask for each deliverable separately. Two applicants then quote in the same terms, and a reviewer can compare them side by side without converting a package price.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Name the person who reviews each kind of application and how they hear about it. Seeding requests can go to whoever packs the boxes, and paid requests to the marketing lead. Name a backup for the weeks that person is away.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Put the offer and the questions into one prompt, along with the rate rule and the people who approve. Emergent builds the influencer application form, the database behind it, and a review screen with approve and decline buttons. Change any question later by asking in plain English.
fields.howto_step_6_title: 06 Close with the terms you expect
fields.howto_step_6_des: Write the posting terms in plain words at the end of the form: the disclosure you expect in each post, how long you may reuse the content, and when posts are due. Ask the applicant to sign before submitting.
fields.howto_step_7_des: Submit one test application under the audience minimum, one with a rate above your approval line, and one that passes both. Check that the first sees the thank-you screen, the second reaches its approver, and the third lands on the shortlist.

faq_plan.q: What is an influencer application form?
faq_plan.a: An influencer application form is the form a brand publishes for creators who want to work with it. It collects each creator's handles and audience per platform, links to past posts, and what they want in return, whether that is free product, a paid rate, or a hosted stay. The brand reviews every application in one place.

faq_plan.q: How do I create an influencer application form?
faq_plan.a: Start by deciding what you offer creators and which details you check before approving one. Describe both in a prompt to Emergent's AI form builder, along with the person who approves each application. Emergent builds the form, the database that stores every application, and a review screen. A new prompt edits any question afterward.

faq_plan.q: What questions should an influencer application form ask?
faq_plan.a: Ask for the creator's name and email, then one row per platform with the handle and audience size. Add their content niche, links to recent sponsored posts, and what they want: product, a rate per deliverable, or a stay. Close with your posting terms. Emergent builds the whole set from a plain-English description, with no response caps.

faq_plan.q: Can one influencer application form handle both gifted and paid collaborations?
faq_plan.a: Yes. Open with a question on the kind of collaboration, then show the rate and deliverable questions only to creators who pick paid. Gifted applicants see a shipping address instead. A coaching application form uses the same branching to separate a free intro call from a paid program.

faq_plan.q: How many followers should an influencer application form require?
faq_plan.a: Set the number from your own program, not a general rule. Look at the creators you already work with and use the smallest audience that still brought results. A minimum can differ by platform, so ask for each platform's count in its own field and compare against that platform's line.

faq_plan.q: What should an influencer application form ask for to verify follower counts?
faq_plan.a: Ask for a link to each profile and a screenshot of the platform's audience insights page, uploaded with the application. Compare the screenshot with the public profile before you approve anyone. Recent posts with comments from real accounts tell you more than the follower number on its own.

faq_plan.q: Can an influencer application form collect tax forms from paid creators?
faq_plan.a: Yes. Add a W-9 upload that appears only after you approve a paid creator, and keep it with their application. The app keeps payment records ready for 1099 reporting; it organizes the data and does not file taxes. A vendor application collects the same form from suppliers before their first invoice.

faq_plan.q: How should an influencer application form explain disclosure rules?
faq_plan.a: Quote the rule in the terms the creator signs. The FTC says the disclosure should be placed with the endorsement message itself. The same page calls it fine, but not necessary, to include a hashtag with the disclosure, such as #ad or #sponsored. It also tells creators not to mix the disclosure into a group of hashtags or links.

faq_plan.q: How long should an influencer application form be?
faq_plan.a: Keep the first screen to what you need for a yes or no: platforms, audience, recent work, and the offer they want. The shipping address and the signed terms close out the application, and only the tax form waits until after approval. With Emergent, every application lands in a database you own, and the W-9 a paid creator uploads later joins the same record.

faq_plan.q: How can an influencer application form show an applicant's past brand partnerships?
faq_plan.a: Add a field for links to 3 recent sponsored posts and the brand each one was for. Open each post, check that the disclosure is there, and read the comments for real engagement. A driver application form asks for driving history in the same spirit: the past record decides the approval.
